learning_outcomes.text: Use of fundamental knowledge in electrotechnics.
Design and coordination of experiments and tests.

The course is taught to second year Electromechanics students. The course addresses notions that will allow future graduates to have a rich background on the design, operation and use of simple electronic circuits (amplifier, voltage stabilizer, harmonic oscillator, switching circuit, logic circuit).
The structure, characteristics and operation of simple electronic circuits (amplifier, voltage stabilizer, harmonic oscillator, switching circuit, logic circuit).

Design and operation of simple electronic circuits such as direct current or alternating current amplifier, voltage stabilizer, LC or RC oscillator, switching circuit (bistable, monostable, stable), respectively logic circuit made in bipolar or unipolar technology.

Developing a positive attitude towards the activities of assimilating new professional knowledge and information, cultivating and promoting a scientific environment focused on values, forming a positive and responsible professional behavior.

syllabus_topics: Basic amplification stages - General (classifications, characteristics, parameters). Stages with a transistor in common-emitter, base-common, common-collector assemblies (parameters and operating characteristics).
Alternating current amplifiers - Schemes, parameters, amplification characteristics, operation.
Direct current amplifiers - Differential amplifier: diagram, operation, characteristic parameters.
Harmonic oscillators I - General; Classifications.
Harmonic oscillators II - LC oscillators (schemes, operation).
Harmonic oscillators III - RC oscillators; Quartz oscillators (schemes, operation).
Switching circuitsI - Switching circuits without memory. Positive reaction in amplifiers (schemes, operation).
Switching circuits II - Tilting circuits with coupling in the emitter (diagrams, operation, characteristics).
Switching circuits III - Tilting circuits with coupling in the base collector: bistable, monostable, stable (diagrams, operation, characteristics).
Logic circuits I - Generalities; Basic logic functions; Simple logic diagrams made with diodes and transistors.
Logic circuits II - Families of logic circuits, made in bipolar or unipolar technology (schemes, operation).
Logic circuits III - Registers, counters (schemes, operation).
Presentation of the content and requirements required for the proper conduct of laboratory work.
Voltage stabilizers.
Alternating current amplifiers.
Differential amplifier.
Oscillators.
Switching circuits.
Logic circuits made in bipolar technology.
Recovery of laboratories. Ending the school situation.

assessment_methods.method: Course evaluation (Oral or written evaluation, online or on-site. Discussions. Argue. Active participation in discussions. Documented arguments. Providing relevant solutions to issues under debate. Knowledge of basics on all topics covered.)

Laboratory written test (minimum of 5). Practical realization of all requirements imposed by all laboratory works. Well-documented arguments. Reading the required bibliography. A percentage of 15% of the final grade at the laboratory is awarded for the successful completion of all the topics provided for individual study.

assessment_rules: Minimum performance standard: obtaining a grade of 5 in each laboratory test; participation and fulfillment of all requirements imposed by each laboratory work; obtaining a grade of 5 in the course tests, as an arithmetic mean of the grades obtained in this type of activity. Knowledge of the basics on all the topics taught.
